subject: physics

moments.title: Gilbert's 'De Magnete'
moments.body: Physician to Queen Elizabeth I, Gilbert publishes the first scientific treatise on magnetism. He shows the Earth itself is a giant magnet, explaining why compasses point north. He coins the term 'electricity' (electricus, from amber).
moments.takeaway: The first quantitative book on electromagnetism, and the first identification of Earth as a magnet.

moments.title: Magnetic survey expeditions
moments.body: Halley charts magnetic declination across the Atlantic. Gauss in 1839 derives the spherical-harmonic decomposition of Earth's field. Magnetic observatories spring up worldwide.
moments.takeaway: Geomagnetism becomes a mature science before its mechanism is understood.

moments.title: Reversals discovered
moments.body: Brunhes finds volcanic rocks magnetised in the wrong direction. The Earth's magnetic field has flipped — and many times. Reversals are confirmed by 1960s seafloor surveys.
moments.takeaway: Earth's poles have flipped hundreds of times. We're 780,000 years overdue for the next.

moments.title: Van Allen belts
moments.body: Explorer 1, the first US satellite, carries Van Allen's Geiger counter. The instrument saturates — Earth has belts of trapped radiation. The discovery essentially launches space physics.
moments.takeaway: Space exploration immediately reveals a new feature of Earth's magnetic environment.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Earth's field is generated by a self-sustaining geodynamo in the liquid outer core. The field has been weakening 5% per century. ESA's Swarm satellite mission monitors it.
now.open_questions: When will Earth's next magnetic reversal occur? Could it harm life or technology?

reflection: Gilbert in 1600 thought magnetism was the 'soul' of the Earth. He was wrong in detail, right in spirit. How should we evaluate metaphors in early science?
